newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to privatise Romtelecom RA telephone firm.
newsitem.headline: Romania to privatise Romtelecom RA telephone firm.

text.p: Romania will launch the privatisation of state telephone company Romtelecom RA this year and is seeking help from a strategic investor, Communications Minister Sorin Pantis said on Tuesday.
"Such an investor would be offered a minority stake in Romtelecom of under 51 percent," Pantis told a news conference.
He said the privatisation process would start by turning the utility into a commercial company over the next three months.
"We also want that investor to get involved in Romtelecom's management," Pantis said.

Romania's privatisation programme, launched in 1995 after long delays, has so far failed to deal with large utilities, including Romtelecom, which form the core of the economy and offer the best hope of attracting big foreign investment.
Romtelecom has the monopoly on telephone services in the Balkan country. It currently employs 55,000 people and has some 2.8 million subscribers across Romania.
The second stage of Romtelecom's privatisation plan would focus on new investments to instal 500,000 new landlines for some 400,000 new subscribers in 1997, Pantis said.

Romtelecom's actual privatisation would start in the first quarter of 1998, Pantis said, adding that his ministry was looking for "a serious international consultant" to evaluate Romtelecom and get involved in its privatisation.
The consultant would be designated through a tender arranged with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), Pantis said.
Auditors Coopers and Lybrand had started to evaluate Romtelecom's 1996 results, to include them in the privatisation offer, ministry sources said.
"Privatisation of Romtelecom could easily attract up to $4.0 billion. It could be one of the biggest businesses in Romania," a ministry official told Reuters recently.
It takes now an average of minimum four years to get a new line installed, ministry data show.

In 1993, the European Investment Bank (EIB) granted the government an 80 million ECU ($100 million) loan to modernise and expand the telecommunications system. Part of the EIB loan was used to build 30 new telephone exchanges and modernise existing ones.
In 1992 the EBRD gave Romtelecom a credit of 142 million ECUs to instal a fibre optic telecommunications network.
